purpose: Help the Brain choose precise, original, context-aware language without copying dictionary entries or publisher style.
boundaries: Do not copy proprietary dictionary definitions.
Do not memorize publisher wording, headlines, or article structure.
Store reusable usage guidance, tone, context, reading level, and editorial preference.
Facts come from Story Dossier; word choice comes from Lexicon Intelligence.

vocabulary.job: Choose words by meaning, context, tone, strength, reading level, and evidence support.

repetitionMonitor.job: Detect overused verbs, transitions, intros, and paragraph moves across News Lab, Creator Desk, and Newsletter.

sentenceIntelligence.job: Vary sentence rhythm and placement without changing facts.

transitionIntelligence.job: Move from fact to context to consequence without repeating the same bridge.

transitionMoves.name: fact-to-context
transitionMoves.guidance: After the verified fact, explain the setting without repeating the headline.

transitionMoves.name: context-to-consequence
transitionMoves.guidance: Move from background to who is affected or what changes next.
avoid: repeating This matters because across paragraphs

transitionMoves.name: source-specific-claim
transitionMoves.guidance: Use source attribution only when a detail is unique or not broadly confirmed.

newsLab: Prefer neutral, evidence-calibrated verbs: confirmed for verified records, alleged for accusations, said/stated for attribution, warned only when risk is explicit.
Avoid opinion-loaded verbs unless the evidence supports them.
Do not mention internal dossiers, source signals, or confidence mechanics in public articles.
creatorDesk: Use stronger opinion language only after the story fact is clear.
Vary transitions so each daily editorial does not sound like the same template.
Prefer precise values language over generic phrases like great, bad, important, or concerning.
newsletter: Rotate openings by week: strongest signal, consequence, what changed, what still needs proof, and what comes next.
Use a magazine-like rhythm with short paragraphs and varied transitions.
Do not repeat the same intro, bridge, or values paragraph from week to week.

writerDirective: Before drafting, choose words by evidence, tone, context, and repetition history. Prefer precise neutral verbs in news, varied values language in Creator Desk, and fresh weekly transitions in Newsletter.
rule: Lexicon Intelligence is a semantic writing system, not a dictionary cache.

behavioralLayer.rule: Use contextual word-choice preferences before drafting. Learn choices, not just words.
